newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK chief Chan faces legal threat in scandal probe.
newsitem.headline: HK chief Chan faces legal threat in scandal probe.

text.p: Hong Kong's top civil servant Anson Chan may face prosecution if she refuses to hand a report on a disgraced former immigration chief to legislators probing his removal, a Hong Kong newspaper said on Wednesday.

The South China Morning Post said the Legislative Council panel, equivalent to a parliamentary select committee, held a closed meeting on Tuesday after hearing Chan had decided not to release a report by graft-busters on Laurence Leung.

"If she still refuses to do so, the committee might condemn her in a full sitting of the council, condemn her in the report of the select committee or ask the Legal Department to prosecute her," panel chairman Ip Kwok-him was quoted as saying.
A spokeswoman for Chan's office said she had not been notified by the panel and declined to comment.

Chan has said it was not in the "public interest" to disclose the ICAC report. She said disclosing the full reports could undermine anti-graft operations in the future by revealing details on how and where sensitive information was gathered.
The report by the Independent Commission Against Corruption formed the basis for the government to force Leung to retire last July.

The government said Leung, 55, had failed to pass an integrity test and to disclose his personal business dealings. The government originally said Leung's sudden departure was due to "personal reasons" but later admitted he was forced out.

The reversal by the government sparked speculation he may have been a Chinese agent as he had access to highly sensitive immigration data on Chinese dissidents taking shelter in Hong Kong or senior government officials who hold foreign passports.
Both Leung and the government denied he was a spy.
Hong Kong reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30, ending more than 150 years of British colonial rule.
